reportOnlyUntil: no apply is authorized: a non-sport checklist source is acquired for these eight sets; every entry here is a PARK and this list routes NOTHING until then
finding: 654 sales of 1950s Topps NON-SPORT cards (Wings, Rails and Sails, Scoop, Look 'n See, Davy Crockett, World on Wheels, Flags of the World, Fighting Marines) are slugged with the vertical segment "baseball" and sit inside 355 pools that otherwise hold real vintage baseball cards. 353 of those 355 pools are genuine baseball cards diluted by non-sport sales; the FMV of every one of them is computed from a comp pool containing cards from a different vertical entirely.
rulings: CF-THE-SPORT-SEGMENT-IS-THE-CARDS-VERTICAL. A 1954 Topps World on Wheels card is not a baseball card. The slug's second segment is the vertical the card belongs to, and "baseball" on a non-sport issue is a wrong identity, not a loose label.

THE GRAMMAR ALLOWS non-sport ALREADY, AND THAT IS NOT ENOUGH. `non-sport` is canonical in CANONICAL_SPORTS (slugGuard.service.ts) and in the Vertical union (resolveVertical.service.ts), so a destination slug is spellable and NOTHING here is invented. But a spellable destination is not a checklist-backed one: card_catalog holds ZERO rows for all eight sets (read-only, 2026-09-06 — zero at cardYear<=1960 for every set phrase, zero at every candidate setKey). Every entry is therefore a PARK, never a RELOCATE.

A REPAIR NEVER MINTS AN IDENTITY FROM A SALE (CF-CATALOG-MATCH-IS-SELF-CONFIRMING). Relocating 654 sales onto slugs no checklist names would create 355 new identities whose only evidence is the sales themselves. The rows are marked identityUnverified and left where they are; the pools stay wrong on purpose until a checklist can say what these cards are.

THE VERTICAL REFACTOR IS NOT THE BLOCKER HERE; THE CHECKLIST IS. The Pokemon expansion is parked on sport->vertical, but that refactor is about RENAMING the segment across the codebase. `non-sport` is already a legal value today, so this list did not need it. What it needs is a non-sport checklist source for eight 1950s Topps issues.

THE TITLE MUST NAME TOPPS, OR THE WORD IS A COINCIDENCE. A first pass on the set phrase alone collected 1,434 rows; 780 of them were false positives — 675 Detroit/Parkhurst RED WINGS hockey cards, 7 1940 Gum Inc Superman "Wings of Mercy", and a T206 "Scoops Carey" (a player nickname). The kept population requires /toppss+<set>/ in the title. Those 780 rows are NOT in this list and were verified individually as correctly-filed cards of their own verticals.

THE YEAR IS NOT THE DEFECT. All 654 rows carry a cardYear equal to their set's real issue year (1952 Wings, 1955 Rails and Sails, 1954 Scoop, 1952 Look 'n See, 1956 Davy Crockett, 1953-55 World on Wheels, 1956 Flags of the World, 1953 Fighting Marines). Only the vertical segment is wrong, on every single row.

census.note: every count point-read against prod read-only on 2026-09-06; pool totals are per-pool COUNT(1) on hobbyiqCardId, partition-bounded

provenance.method: title phrase + /toppss+<set>/ attestation, cardYear<=1960, then per-pool COUNT and per-destination card_catalog point-read
